'''Fishing''' is the act of catching items with a [[Fishing Rod|fishing rod]]. Matcha Flavoured replaces the vanilla fishing loot with a biome-based system: the water's biome decides which of 11 climate tables a catch comes from, and each climate has 5 fish of different rarity. With the [[Fisherman]] paying [[Obol]]s for fish, fishing is one of the few ways to earn money in the pack.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=Fisherman are the only villager that will buy items from you and pay handsomely. So, even if you fish for a bit, fail to catch any treasure, you can still take home a few bucks when you get back to your base.}}</ref>

The pack has 47 different [[fish]] to catch, not counting the frogs, tadpoles and axolotls that can turn up as [[fishing junk]].

== Mechanics ==
Casting, waiting, bite timing, {{MCW|Lure}} and the "open water" check all work as in vanilla. Only the loot tables are changed.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing.json}}</ref>

=== Choosing the catch ===
Each catch rolls the <code>gameplay/fishing</code> loot table once. It picks one of three categories: junk, treasure or the biome's table. Since {{Version|1.12.7-beta}} the biome tables are the children of one <code>alternatives</code> entry, which gives the first table whose biome matches the bobber: the climate and special-biome tables in turn, then temperate saltwater for any biome in the pack's <code>#minecraft:fallback</code> tag, and otherwise the junk table (see [[#Other biomes]]).<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing.json}}</ref>

The pack writes a weight of 85 and a quality of −1 on the <code>alternatives</code> entry, but in ''Minecraft'' 26.3 a composite entry has no weight or quality: only its children do, and the biome tables have none set, so the chosen one weighs 1 with quality 0.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing.json}}</ref> In open water a catch is therefore junk 10 times in 16 (62.5%), treasure 5 times in 16 (31.25%) and from the biome's table only 1 time in 16 (6.25%). Out of open water it is junk 10 times in 11 (90.91%) and the biome's table 1 time in 11 (9.09%). This is listed on [[Known bugs]].

{{Data/Fishing/Categories}}

If the bobber isn't in open water, treasure can't be caught, and junk and the biome's table share its weight.

Each level of {{MCW|Luck of the Sea}} adds the entry's quality to its weight, as in vanilla. The pack doesn't change what the enchantment does, only its anvil cost.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/enchantment/luck_of_the_sea.json}}</ref> The table gives the odds at each level, in and out of open water, for each group of biomes that share the same entries.

{{Data/Fishing/Luck}}

Luck of the Sea doesn't change how often fish are caught in open water: each level moves 2 weight from junk to treasure, and the biome's table keeps its weight of 1. With Luck of the Sea III a catch in open water is junk 25%, treasure 68.75% and fish 6.25% of the time. Inside the climate tables the fish have no quality, so it doesn't change which fish is caught or its star rating either. The {{Version|1.12.7-beta}} notes say that Luck of the Sea now affects the star rating of fish, but nothing in the pack does that.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.7-beta|quote=Luck of the Sea now affects the quality (Star rating) of fish caught}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/freshwater_cold.json}}</ref>

=== Rarity ===
Every caught fish has a rarity of 1 to 4 stars, shown as the first line of its tooltip (⭐☆☆☆, ⭐⭐☆☆, ⭐⭐⭐☆ or ⭐⭐⭐⭐, in gray, green, aqua and pink).<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json}}</ref> Every freshwater and saltwater climate has the same layout:

{{Data/Fishing/Rarity}}

The two fish of the special biomes don't follow the table: the [[Creaking Fish]] (⭐⭐⭐☆) sells at 2 for 1 Obol and only once the Fisherman is a Master, and the [[Echo Eel]] (⭐⭐⭐⭐) sells like the other epic fish.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/villager_trade/fisherman/5/pale_fish.json}}</ref>

The developer grouped the fish this way so that every climate earns about the same amount of money.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.5-alpha|quote=Each biome/water type have 5 fish, two common, one uncommon, one rare, and one epic. [...] This was done to better balance the selling system, so each biome will be just as "efficient" to fish in as any other}}</ref> The rarity is part of the item and only the fishing loot tables add it, so only fish from those tables can be sold. A [[cod]] dropped by a mob doesn't carry the rarity line and can't be sold.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.5-alpha|quote=Cod and Salmon cannot be killed and sold, only if caught will they be valid.}}</ref>

=== Fish are cod, salmon and pufferfish ===
Every custom fish is a vanilla {{MCW|Raw Cod|cod}}, {{MCW|Raw Salmon|salmon}} or {{MCW|Pufferfish|pufferfish}} with its own name, texture and rarity line. Small fish are cod and cook into [[Cooked Fish|cooked fish]]. Large fish are salmon and cook into [[Cooked Large Fish|cooked large fish]]. The [[Freshwater Puffer]] is a pufferfish and cooks into [[Cooked Pufferfish|cooked pufferfish]]. See [[Fish]] for the full list.

== Climates ==
The climate table is chosen by the biome at the bobber. Each table below lists the fish, the rarity, the weight inside the table and the chance of that fish per cast with no Luck of the Sea. "Open water" is the normal case. "Other water" is a small or enclosed pool, where treasure can't be caught.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/worldgen/biome/freshwater_cold.json}}</ref>

The biome groups are defined by the pack's biome tags (<code>#minecraft:freshwater_cold</code> and so on). The [[Angler's Almanac]] shows the same groups under the names given in italics.

{{Diagram|Fishing climates|caption=The climate tables from cold to hot: a few of the biomes each one covers, and its fish from common to rare.}}

They do have their own junk: [[Frog|frogs]] and [[Tadpole|tadpoles]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/swamps.json}}</ref>

=== Special biomes ===
Three biomes have small tables of their own. Pale Garden and Deep Dark mix one fish with biome items, and Sulfur Caves has no fish.

{{Data/Fishing/Special biomes}}
<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/pale_garden.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/deep_dark.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/sulfur_caves.json}}</ref>

Until {{Version|1.12.7-beta}} Deep Dark and Sulfur Caves were also in the pack's <code>#minecraft:unused</code> biome tag, which added a second junk entry of weight 85, so about half of all catches there were junk. 1.12.7-beta deleted the tag, and the three special biomes now work like the climates.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/worldgen/biome/unused.json|at=fe225857ed8af507b7f5755f4d41678f6862b1bd}}</ref>

Before 1.12.3 the fish bones from the Sulfur Caves table had the wrong item model, so they showed the missing-model texture and didn't stack with fish bones from the junk table. See [[Fish Bones]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/sulfur_caves.json}}</ref>

=== Other biomes ===
Mushroom Fields, the [[Hell]] biomes and [[The End]] biomes have no fish. They get the last child of the biome entry, the junk table, so in open water a catch there is junk 11 times in 16 (68.75%) and treasure 5 times in 16 (31.25%).<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing.json}}</ref> The {{Version|1.10}} notes meant this fallback junk to have a weight of 85.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.10|quote=Fishing outside of pre-designated biomes no longer gives insane loot (junk pool at 85 weight as fallback)}}</ref>

Since {{Version|1.12.7-beta}} Snowy Beach is in the cold freshwater tag, and Dappled Forest in the temperate freshwater tag; before, they were in no biome tag, so only the base junk (10) and treasure (5) entries applied there.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/worldgen/biome/freshwater_cold.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/worldgen/biome/freshwater_temperate.json}}</ref> Biomes added by other packs or mods are in none of the pack's climate tags. Those in an ocean or beach tag (<code>#minecraft:is_ocean</code>, <code>#minecraft:is_beach</code> or the common <code>#c:is_ocean</code> and <code>#c:is_beach</code>) use the temperate saltwater table through <code>#minecraft:fallback</code>, and the others get the fallback junk.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/worldgen/biome/fallback.json}}</ref> Every vanilla ocean and beach already has a climate, so the fallback tag only matters for modded biomes. The {{Version|1.12.5}} notes said the junk fix was "not for modded biomes".<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.5|quote=Fishing Junk LT Fixed (Not for modded biomes)}}</ref>

== Junk and treasure ==
{{Main|Fishing junk|Fishing treasure}}
Junk is mostly lily pads, [[Sturdy Leather|leather]], [[Fish Bones|fish bones]], water bottles, [[Estus Ash]] and nautilus shells. Some biomes add their own junk: [[bamboo]] in jungles, [[Frog|frogs]] and [[Tadpole|tadpoles]] in swamps, and [[Axolotl|axolotls]] in Dripstone Caves and Lush Caves.

Treasure is [[Obol]]s, enchanted fishing rods, [[Hell-Bound Book]]s, goat horns, angler pottery sherds, [[Crystal Heart]]s and rarely a chest of buried treasure.

== Selling fish ==
The [[Fisherman]] is the only villager who buys fish. He pays 1 Obol for a set number of caught fish, depending on rarity (see the tables above). Fish of a higher rarity only become sellable as the Fisherman levels up, so trading the common fish is what unlocks the rare ones.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.5-alpha|quote=The Fisherman selling system has been reworked so you have to sell lower-tier fish before you can sell higher tier fish, this was to prevent fish-related "spoilers"}}</ref> At Novice level he sells the [[Angler's Almanac]] for 1 Obol.

{{Data/Trades/Fisherman}}

== Cooking ==
Fish heal only once cooked. Raw fish can still be eaten, but they restore no health, and pufferfish still poison the player (see [[Pufferfish]]).
{| class="wikitable"
! Raw fish !! Result !! Heals !! Stations
|-
| Small fish ([[cod]]-based) and {{ItemLink|Tropical Fish}} || {{ItemLink|Cooked Fish}} || {{Value|Cooked Fish|heals}} || [[Oven]], [[Kindling]]
|-
| Large fish ([[salmon]]-based) || {{ItemLink|Cooked Large Fish}} || {{Value|Cooked Large Fish|heals}} || Oven, Kindling
|-
| {{ItemLink|Pufferfish}}, {{ItemLink|Freshwater Puffer}} || {{ItemLink|Cooked Pufferfish}} || {{Value|Cooked Pufferfish|heals}} and [[Conduit Power]] ({{Value|Cooked Pufferfish|duration|effect=Conduit Power|format=clock}}) || Oven, Kindling
|-
| Any fish || {{ItemLink|Charred Fish}} || {{Value|Charred Fish|heals}} || [[Mud Kiln]]
|}

== Other sources of fishing loot ==
The {{MCW|Elder Guardian|elder guardian}}'s drops roll the fishing table 3 times, using the biome where it dies. It isn't a fishing bobber, so these rolls never give treasure.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/entities/elder_guardian.json}}</ref> The village fisherman's house chest table, which rolled it too, is empty.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/chests/village/village_fisher.json}}</ref>

== Sounds ==
{{Main|Fishing sounds}}
Each catch plays a sound for its category: one per star rating, one each for junk and treasure, and special ones for fish bones, axolotls, frogs and tadpoles, nautilus shells and Hell-Bound Books.

== Advancements ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Advancement !! Description !! Requirement !! Reward
|-
| '''Fishmonger''' || Sell caught fish to a Fisherman || Trade with a Fisherman and receive an Obol. || 1 [[Obol]]
|-
| '''No More Fish in the Sea''' || Catch Everything! || Catch all 47 fish with a fishing rod. A challenge that follows Fishmonger. || 10 Obols

<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/tutorial/catch_everything.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/tutorial/trade_fish.json}}</ref>

The [[Angler's Almanac]] adds its own advancement tab with an entry for every catch. Before 1.12.3 the pufferfish entry in Hot Saltwater couldn't be unlocked.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/anglers_almanac/saltwater/hot/pufferfish.json}}</ref> In 1.12.4 the junk entries, apart from Fish Bones, couldn't be unlocked, because nothing could be caught from the junk table.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/junk.json|at=acec32328368f3985c45f8077732d92a664f3d13}}</ref> Since 1.12.5 they can, and since 1.12.6-alpha the junk table's fish bones, which used to be ender pearls, also complete the Fish Bones entry.

Swamps get their own table and junk.
Added [[Cooked Pufferfish|cooked pufferfish]].
Crystal Hearts added to fishing treasure.}}
{{History line|1.02|Added a fishing advancement.}}
{{History line|1.10|Fish needed per Obol lowered: ⭐ 24 → 12, ⭐⭐ 12 → 8, ⭐⭐⭐ 8 → 4, ⭐⭐⭐⭐ unchanged at 1.
Biomes outside the climates now fall back to a junk entry of weight 85.
Treasure rebalanced: chests and Crystal Hearts rarer, enchanted fishing rods more common.
Echo Eel and Creaking Fish buffed, since lakes don't generate in their biomes.
Fixed tropical freshwater being overridden by arid freshwater.
The Opah can now be sold.
The Alaska Blackfish now counts for No More Fish in the Sea (its name was misspelled in the advancement).}}
{{History line|1.12|Fishing buried treasure buffed slightly.}}
{{History line|1.12.1-alpha|Added the [[Angler's Almanac]] and [[Fishing sounds|fishing sounds]].
Fish changed to the current item format. Fish caught before this version can no longer be sold.
Fish now make up 85 of 100 weight in their biomes (a previous patch gave junk about 50% of the time).

Old Growth Spruce Taiga added to cool freshwater.}}
{{History line|1.12.2|The Angler's Almanac entries for Warm Saltwater and for the axolotl can be unlocked.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/anglers_almanac/saltwater/warm/root.json}}</ref>}}
{{History line|1.12.3|2=Fish Bones caught in Sulfur Caves now have the correct texture.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/sulfur_caves.json}}</ref> The Angler's Almanac entry for pufferfish in Hot Saltwater can be unlocked.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/anglers_almanac/saltwater/hot/pufferfish.json}}</ref>}}
{{History line|1.12.4|The junk table can't be loaded, so junk catches give nothing.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/junk.json|at=acec32328368f3985c45f8077732d92a664f3d13}}</ref>}}

{{History line|1.12.6-alpha|The village fisherman's house chest table no longer rolls the fishing table.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/chests/village/village_fisher.json}}</ref>}}
{{History line|1.12.7-beta|The biome tables were put into one <code>alternatives</code> entry that picks the first matching table, with temperate saltwater for modded ocean and beach biomes (<code>#minecraft:fallback</code>) and junk for the rest. }}

== Trivia ==
* The developer planned a legendary tier of fish caught only under special conditions (rain, night, full moon) and more fish for the magical biomes.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.5-alpha|quote=I want a new legendary fish tier caught only under specific conditions (Raining, night, full moon, etc)}}</ref>
* In the introduction video the developer describes "almost 50 different fish you can catch, including frogs". The code has 47 fish.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=Almost 50 different fish you can catch, including frogs.}}</ref>
